q: How do I calculate the CO2 from incinerating waste?
title: Waste incineration fossil CO2
short: Use IPCC Equation 5.1: waste burnt x dry matter share x carbon share x fossil carbon share x oxidation factor x 44/12. Only fossil carbon, mainly from plastics and synthetics, counts in the CO2 total; carbon in food, paper and wood is biogenic.
audience: Waste generators, incinerator operators and hospitals

ul: Tonnes of each waste type burnt, from the operator's records.
Dry matter, carbon and fossil carbon fractions: measured, or IPCC defaults.
Oxidation factor: 1.0 for incineration by IPCC default.

p: If you run the incinerator, its CO2 is Scope 1. Waste sent to an outside incinerator or waste-to-energy plant is Scope 3, Category 5 for the generator.
Food, paper and wood carbon is biogenic, so its CO2 is reported outside the scopes. Methane and N2O from incineration are small and calculated separately.

example.title: Worked example: plastic waste incinerated (illustrative inputs)
lines: IPCC defaults for plastics: dry matter 100 percent, carbon 75 percent of dry matter, fossil carbon 100 percent, oxidation 1.0
example.note: Fractions are IPCC 2006 defaults for plastics (Volume 5, Table 2.4); use measured values where available.

senseible: Senseible keeps waste manifests, transport invoices and treatment bills as evidence on the Scope 3 trail and reads electricity bills for on-site equipment into Scope 2. Avoided emissions are never subtracted from the inventory.
